claim: Papers > Permission To Work > OPT 'Apply For OPT' / 'Apply With Premium Processing', and the 'Your US Status Is Ending' decision's two actions, standard and premium by name, run documents.apply_opt. optRefusal refuses a citizen, someone with no F-1, someone who left without the degree, applications outside the window from 90 days before to 60 after the program's end, and a second application. It charges $470, or $2,250 with premium, from the bank, pushes a pending OPT permit, and schedules PERMISSION_KIND at +90 days, or 30 business days with premium. It resolves the open us-status decision. claim: Papers > Benefits 'File A Claim' runs benefits.claim. The button is hidden while studying, without permission to work, or with a short base period. Britain, Ireland and Mexico City route to their own claims. In the US the state is the base-period wages' state, or else the home state. The claim is refused when one is open, for a CT full-time student (CGS 31-235(b)), and for a non-citizen without a US work permit (FUTA). The monetary test runs on the basic or alternate base period. The command records the claim (CT has no waiting week) and schedules BENEFIT_WEEK_KIND for the next Sunday at 8 PM. Each week checks availability, reduces the benefit by the week's work (workedBetween -> weekBenefit), applies the waiting week, posts to the payee account and records the benefit through recordBenefit (yearOf().unemployment, the unearned kind). The claim closes at maxTotal or after a year. The return counts it as income.

claim: 'File It' on the Returns tab, or the decision 'Your <year> Tax Return' made each February, runs tax.file. It does these things: refigures the year (figuresFor); sets filedAt and the late penalty; resolves the decision; files each state's side; then the IRS side. That side is a refund scheduled 21 days on (plus ITIN weeks for a 1040-NR without an SSN), or the balance with penalty and interest paid from the bank, or, if the bank can't pay, owed with collection begun. It also cancels a pending substitute return. A substitute already assessed is reconsidered instead.
